newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Glaxo Wellcome profit seen rising.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Glaxo Wellcome profit seen rising.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc, the world's biggest drugs company, is expected to announce a sharp rise in 1996 pre-tax profits on March 6, but analysts said on Friday that their gaze would be fixed firmly on prospects for the current, highly critical year.
Analysts expect the group to report pre-tax profit of between 2.913 and 3.005 billion stg, compared with 2.505 a year earlier.

However, analysts said this would be the last big leap in profits for a while, with the group working hard to stand still in 1997 as it tackles the expiry of key patents on its top-selling drugs, anti-ulcerant Zantac and herpes treatment Zovirax.
Zantac, which had sales of nearly 2.3 billion stg in 1995, is set to lose its U.S. and British patents in July.
The Zantac expiry means that Glaxo Wellcome will face generic competition on around 10 percent of its total sales by the middle of the year, with a rapid erosion of its position widely expected.

Analysts will be interested in the extent to which Glaxo Wellcome is able to imitate SmithKline Beecham, where rapid growth in other products masked the patent loss of the group's best-seller Tagamet.

The performance of newer drugs will therefore be watched particularly closely on March 6. Analysts said there were signs that products such as Migraine treatment Imigran, the newly rejuvenated AIDS drug Retrovir and the fast-growing respiratory franchise will take up the slack left by Zantac and Zovirax faster than expected.

Sales of Retrovir, in particular, are expected to have risen dramatically after the drug's success in combination with other drugs, where HIV virus levels have been reduced to virtually undetectable levels.
